small_guidance:
- Add `triton.autotune` over BLOCK_N ∈ {64, 128, 256, 512}, num_warps ∈ {4, 8}, num_stages ∈ {2, 3} keyed on (OD, OH, OW); current fixed BLOCK_N=256/4 warps is likely under-tuned for OH*OW=62*62.
- Tile spatial along OW only (one program per (n, oc, od, oh) row of length OW=62) so input loads along iw are contiguous and reusable across kw — replaces the strided gather pattern caused by linearizing OD*OH*OW.
- Hoist the `(pid_n*IC+ic)*ID` and `(pid_oc*IC+ic)*KD` base offsets out of the inner loops, and unroll KD/KH/KW (all =3) with `tl.static_range` to cut index arithmetic.
large_guidance:
- Restructure as an implicit-GEMM: one program per (N, OC-tile, spatial-tile) with BLOCK_OC=16/32, BLOCK_S=64/128, reduction K=IC*KD*KH*KW=81; use `tl.dot` on a [BLOCK_S, BLOCK_K] × [BLOCK_K, BLOCK_OC] tile so the compiler uses tensor cores and reuses input loads across output channels (currently each (oc) reloads x independently).
- Alternatively, switch to channels-last (NDHWC) layout and load a vector of all 16 output channels at once per spatial point — IC*KD*KH*KW=81 reductions feeding 16 OC outputs maximizes weight/input reuse per loaded x value.
- Fuse the epilogue (scale, tanh via `(e2-1)/(e2+1)`, bias mul, sigmoid) on the accumulator register tile before store — already done; keep this and ensure the OC broadcast of scale/bias is loaded once per program.
